description: Kwongan shrubland and Allocasuarina huegeliana / Eucalyptus wandoo woodland
locality: Tutanning Nature Reserve, 150 km east-south-east of Perth, western wheatbelt (Avon Wheatbelt Bioregion), Western Australia
vegetation: Isolated 2140-ha remnant containing a mosaic of vegetation, including Eucalyptus and Allocasuarina woodlands, granite outcrop herbfields and shrublands, and kwongan shrublands
climate description: Dry Mediterranean; rainfall mainly in winter from May to September
fire history: Experimental fires: April 1985 (44 ha of kwongan and woodland, previously burnt 1960; 21 plots, resampled to 2015) and March 1990 (108 ha, previously burnt 1965; 45 plots, resampled to 2000)
fire intensity: 1985 fire moderate intensity, hot in patches; 1990 fire moderate to high intensity (1100 m/h in kwongan, 200 m/h with 2 m flame height in Allocasuarina woodland, 100 m/h in Eucalyptus woodland, where the canopy remained unburnt)
notes: Coordinates 32°33'S, 117°20'E as printed (Methods p.340), converted to decimal degrees. Climate from Pingelly, 20 km west of Tutanning (rainfall since 1891; BoM, accessed 22 January 2016). Plots: 66 x 100-m2 circular plots (43 in woodland, 23 in kwongan) across the two fires; data from both fires were combined into a single time-since-fire series, and vegetation type was not analysed separately (50% of species shared by kwongan and woodland).
